ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 8082, as amended, the FTRA); Enforcement Decree of the FTRA; Financial Services Commission and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit supervisory regulations; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Certain Regulations on the Protection of Financial Privacy; Commercial Act and the Enforcement Decree provisions relating to corporate registration and shareholder identification; Beneficial ownership information is not maintained in a public UBO register for Yuhan Hoesa but is collected by financial institutions under the FTRA and reported to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU), making the disclosure level Government-Only-Access.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Foreign Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry in the country of origin of the foreign parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the origin country is an Apostille Hague Convention State: notarize by local notary, obtain Apostille from the origin country competent authority, translate into Korean, and submit to Korean registry. If the origin country is not an Apostille State: notarize and then obtain consular legalization through the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea in that country. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Existence of the Foreign Parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or tax authority in the foreign parent's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize in the foreign parent's jurisdiction; if Apostille Convention member, affix Apostille from the member state competent authority; if non-member, obtain consular legalization from the Republic of Korea embassy or consulate. Use only the path applicable to the origin country; never combine Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney Appointing the Korean Incorporation Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent's board of directors, certified by the corporate secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sign before a notary in the parent's jurisdiction; for Apostille Convention states, attach an Apostille issued by the competent authority; for non-member states, complete consular legalization at the Republic of Korea embassy or consulate. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must not be applied in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or Memorandum of Association of the Foreign Parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent company as registered with its local corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy notarized by a notary in the origin jurisdiction; Apostille if origin is a Hague member; consular legalization if origin is not a member. Do not attach both an Apostille and a consular legalization to the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Foreign Parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issuing bank confirms authenticity; bank-authorized signature must be notarized; then either Apostille by the competent authority for Hague member states or consular legalization by the Republic of Korea consulate for non-member states. Apostille and consular legalization are separate, non-combinable routes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport and Proof of Address of Each Ultimate Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Immigration authority, passport office, or public records office in the UBO's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Copy of passport and utility or government-issued address proof must be notarized locally; if the UBO's country is an Apostille Contracting State, obtain Apostille; if not, obtain consular legalization from the Republic of Korea embassy or consulate. Select only one authentication path based on country.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, US OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT sanctions list, Republic of Korea domestic designation list maintained by the Ministry of Economy and Finance and KoFIU, and Interpol notices. Perform automated fuzzy-matching screening at onboarding, adverse-media review, and continuous 90-day rescreening. For any identified or self-declared PEP, including heads of state, senior politicians, senior judges, senior military officers, immediate family members, and close associates, apply enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, senior management approval, and intensified transaction monitoring. Confirmed matches require freezing assets, filing a suspicious transaction report with KoFIU within 24 hours, and terminating or rejecting the client relationship until clearance is obtained.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IROS) of the Supreme Court of Korea, accessible at https://iros.go.kr, used for corporation registration and name verification; supplementary use of Hometax for business registration and trade name confirmation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Korean Yuhan Hoesa must have a legal corporate name in Hangul, the local Korean script, and must conclude with the legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa for a limited liability company. A Latin-script trade name may be registered separately, but any foreign-language name must be phonetically transliterated into Hangul under the National Institute of Korean Language loanword orthography. The four-tier naming convention requires checking: (1) exact identity with an existing registered name in the same registry; (2) substantial similarity of the distinctive part when altered only by numbers, particles, symbols, spacing, or slight transliteration changes; (3) misleading association with public authorities, financial industries, or licensed professions; and (4) consistency between the chosen name and the Yuhan Hoesa legal form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal, obtain the written rejection note from the registration officer identifying the grounds for refusal. Within the statutory appeal period normally stated in the rejection note, which is typically one month, file a written objection with the head judge of the district court having jurisdiction over the registry, attaching the rejection note, the proposed articles of incorporation, and a Korean legal opinion on name distinguishability. The court may order the registration officer to accept the application if the objection is upheld. In parallel, the applicant may file a fresh application using an altered distinctive mark, numeric modifier, or revised transliteration to avoid identity confusion. Korean-language pleadings prepared by local counsel are mandatory for the objection procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a data-labeling and AI-training BPO in Korea, a pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is materially likely to be rejected by banks for corporate account opening and treated as deficient by the National Tax Service for Hometax registration because the business requires physical or controlled data-processing infrastructure, secure data handling, staff presence, and records under the Personal Information Protection Act. The Korean court registry may accept a registered agent address for registration, but financial institutions performing AML/KYC will view a mailbox-only address as a high-risk red flag. A serviced office with a dedicated lease in the company name, at least one workable desk, utility and internet bills, and a compliance contact is the minimum acceptable commercial substance for this BPO.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection by the municipal tax office or registry authorities is approximately 18% within the first 24 months and increases to 35% if annual VAT-able revenue exceeds KRW 100 million or if the company claims significant VAT refunds. Inspection checklist includes: actual staff presence, workstation and internet connectivity, data processing equipment, signed lease agreement in the company's name, utility and communication invoices, visible corporate signage or name plate, corporate records and seal, privacy and data security policies as required by the Personal Information Protection Act, and a data processing room or secure server/cloud evidence. If multiple checklist items fail, the authorities may deregister the office or impose a business suspension.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Part II, Chapter VIII, Articles 543 through 613 (Yuhan Hoesa / Korean limited company), together with Article 172 governing the effective date of incorporation upon registration and the Commercial Registration Act and Court Registration Fee Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the Company in the Republic of Korea; online filings processed through the Supreme Court I-ROGO electronic registration system.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certified Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa, filed together with the executed Korean-language Articles of Incorporation, certificate of full contribution payment, statements of acceptance by directors and statutory auditor, evidence of registered office, and corporate seal registration application.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act. However, all contribution units must be fully paid at formation. Cash contributions must be deposited in a licensed Korean bank formation deposit account and evidenced by a certificate of contribution payment issued by such bank. Non-cash contributions are permitted if valued in accordance with the Commercial Act. No blocked governmental escrow or capital maintenance account is required. A non-resident investor may need to file a foreign direct investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and remit through a licensed foreign exchange bank.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS AND MEMBERS OF YUHANGHOESA. WHEREAS the undersigned initial members have adopted the Articles of Incorporation and the Company is being formed as a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea; WHEREAS the entire stated capital of the Company has been fully subscribed and paid by the initial members as set forth in the contribution payment certificate; WHEREAS the initial directors have been elected in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation; and WHEREAS the Korean Commercial Act requires the initial governance body to address capital subscription, banking authority, the registered office, and the selection of statutory officers before the Company begins business. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED as follows: 1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: The stated capital of the Company, KRW ___ , has been lawfully subscribed by the initial members and fully paid into the Company formation account at the bank. The Board accepts the subscription and records the contribution units of each member in the register of members. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The registered office and principal place of business is fixed at the address in the Republic of Korea as stated in the Articles of Incorporation. The CEO is instructed to execute the office lease, register the address, and file all amendments with the court registrar and tax authority. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Representative Director and legal counsel are authorized to open the Corporation operational bank account. The bank shall list the Representative Director and the Chief Financial Officer as authorized signatories; any single signature shall be valid for domestic transactions up to KRW ?? and any transaction exceeding such amount requires two signatures. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The following persons are duly appointed: as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, as Director and Chief Operating Officer, and as Statutory Auditor. Each appointee accepts the office and will serve until the first annual members meeting or until a successor is lawfully appointed. 5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The CEO and corporate counsel are jointly and severally authorized to complete incorporation registration, pay all court and stamp fees, apply for the corporate business registration certificate, and take every lawful action required to vest the Company with legal existence and operational capacity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Predetermination and Execution of Korean-Language Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea I-ROGO Online Corporate Registration System; Commercial Registration Division of the relevant District Court for name review.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an official corporate name search in I-ROGO to ensure the proposed name is not identical to, or deceptively similar to, an already registered Korean company. Draft the Korean Articles of Incorporation specifying the corporate name with the Yuhan Hoesa ending, the exact registered office address within a city or county, the corporate purpose covering data labeling, artificial intelligence training data curation, reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), and business process outsourcing (BPO); the total stated capital and contribution units; the name and contribution of each initial member; the method of contribution payment; the number of directors and auditor; and the duration of the company. Every founder or legally authorized attorney must sign and seal the articles. Provide a sworn Korean Power of Attorney notarized overseas if a non-resident member is unable to attend; an apostilled certificate is required if the issuer is a Hague Abolition country.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name check result printout
Executed Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Identification of each member - foreign passport or resident registration card
Notarized and apostilled power of attorney for any authorized representative
Statement of contribution units and member names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is prohibited because of name duplication, select a fresh name and amend the articles before filing; if a document is formally defective, cure by correcting and re-executing under the Commercial Act amendment process before the expiration of the statutory defect-cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Formation Deposit Account and Full Payment of Contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed foreign exchange bank in the Republic of Korea, including KB, Shinhan, Hana, Woori, or similar depository institution; Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency for foreign direct investment reporting, if applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional company formation account under the name of the entity being incorporated at a licensed Korean bank. Each member transfers his or her cash contribution in Korean Won to this account from a domestic or foreign bank account. For a non-resident member, report foreign direct investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and remit through a foreign exchange bank. Request the bank to issue a certificate of contribution payment. The certificate must identify the payer, the account, the amount, and the account owner name. The funds must remain in the account until the registration application is filed and may be disbursed only after the corporate registration certificate has been issued.
required_dossiers: Provisional bank account application
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Contributor and member identification documents
Foreign investment report and remittance receipts for non-resident members
Address and contact details of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses opening because of a defective company name or address, revise the draft articles and resubmit; if foreign exchange documentation is incomplete, use the domestic exchange bank non-trade remittance correction procedure or re-remit after compliance review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing for Incorporation Registration with District Court Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court for the area where the registered office is located; electronic submission via the Supreme Court I-ROGO internet registration office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company by submitting the completed application for registration of incorporation electronically through I-ROGO or in person at the registry. The court will review the application, the executed articles, the bank certificate evidencing full contribution payment, the certificate of registered office use or consent of the building owner, the written acceptance of appointment by each director and statutory auditor, the corporate seal registration application, the power of attorney, and the payment of court fees. If the court issues a suspension or a correction request within two weeks, submit the corrected instrument. Upon confirmation, the court issues the corporate registry extract evidencing legal existence.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Registration of Incorporation
Executed Korean-language Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of full contribution payment issued by the bank
Certificate of registered office location or consent of building owner
Written acceptance of director and statutory auditor appointments
Corporate seal registration application and seal impression
Power of attorney and nationality documents
Court registration fee payment reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order, submit a corrective supplement through I-ROGO within 14 days; a new application and additional fees are required only where the defect is fundamental and cannot be cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Business Registration Certificate and Corporate Identification Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office under the National Tax Service; online filing through the National Tax Service HomeTax system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the court registration extract, file the business registration application within twenty-one days of incorporation. Attach the corporate registry extract, certificate of corporate seal impression, directors identification, the lease or utility bill evidencing the registered office, and the completed business registration application form. The district tax office will issue a business registration certificate with a unique Korean business registration number. This certificate is required for VAT registration, tax invoices, withholding, payroll, and permanent bank account opening. The applicant must also report the actual place of business to the competent employment and labor office if employees will be hired.
required_dossiers: Corporate Registry Extract
Certificate of corporate seal impression
Directors identification documents
Registered office lease or utility bill
Business registration application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If business registration is queried or rejected, file a correction application with the district tax officer and complete any missing exhibits; if rejected for tax clearance issues, remedy by paying any outstanding national taxes and submitting the official tax payment certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Operating Bank Account, Corporate Seal Registration and Post-Incorporation Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in the Republic of Korea; National Tax Service; National Pension Service; National Health Insurance Service; Employment and Labor Insurance offices for mandatory social insurance registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the permanent operating corporate bank account and transfer the formation deposit into it; register the corporate seal with the bank and obtain a certificate of corporate seal impression. Apply for the four mandatory social insurances at the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, and Employment and Labor Insurance offices if employees will be employed, and issue payroll and employment records. Execute the office lease and any corporate credit card applications, update the business registration with any changed contact details, and file the completed incorporation and business registration documents in the corporate governance binder. All filings must be recorded in the company resolution book.
required_dossiers: Corporate Registry Extract
Business Registration Certificate
Corporate seal
Passport and resident registration of representative director
Completed bank account application form
Four major insurance registration forms and employment list
Certificates demonstrating compliance with tax and insurance authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses onboarding, provide an updated beneficial owner declaration and comply with KYC and AML enhanced due diligence; if insurance authorities reject because of omitted employees, submit amended payroll and employment records within the statutory correction period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no physical industrial, manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing activity; data labeling and AI training BPO is an office-based digital services operation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no statutory industrial operating license or special permit is required for the scope of data labeling, RLHF data curation, and BPO activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - ISIC 8220 and NAICS 518210 represent an information and back-office service sector; no physical installation requiring an environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater, volatile organic compounds, hazardous waste, stack emissions, or stationary source discharge will be generated by the licensed office operation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defense fire permit is required for a non-warehousing office or digital services operation; standard workplace safety duties under the Korean Occupational Safety and Health Act and general office fire safety under the Fire Services Act apply and are satisfied by the building fire safety certificate and employer compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax System (https://www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Korean Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), the entity must complete business registration with the competent district tax office through the HomeTax system or in-person submission within 20 days of commencing business. The application must include articles of incorporation, certificate of corporate registration, lease agreement or ownership document proving the Korean place of business, identity documentation of the representative director, and bank account confirmation. The NTS will issue the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which simultaneously functions as the Corporate Taxpayer Identification Number and the VAT registration number. For a foreign non-resident enterprise without a fixed Korean place of business that makes taxable supplies in Korea, Korean VAT law requires the appointment of a domestic tax representative, who must file the same business registration application in the foreign entity's name via HomeTax, attaching a power of attorney, documents proving the foreign entity's legal existence, and evidence of the foreign entity's place of management, after which the NTS issues a business registration number for non-resident taxpayers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not provide check-the-box elections or dedicated hybrid mismatch elections. A Yuhan Hoesa is automatically treated as a separate taxable legal entity for both corporate income tax and value added tax purposes. No entity-level classification election or pass-through election is available under the Corporate Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No mandatory turnover threshold for corporations; every business making taxable supplies in Korea must register for VAT before commencing business. The simplified VAT regime may apply to certain small individual businesses with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80,000,000, but registration remains mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices issued to other businesses must be transmitted electronically as e-tax invoices through the HomeTax system, which assigns a unique digital approval number to each valid e-tax invoice. Submission may be made via the HomeTax portal directly or through approved ERP-to-NTS API/XML channels. E-tax invoice issuance is also mandatory for zero-rated export transactions. For B2C taxable supplies, cash receipts must be issued under the Cash Receipt System, and all relevant transaction data must be reported to the NTS in the prescribed electronic format. Failure to issue and transmit e-tax invoices subjects the taxpayer to statutory penalty surcharges under the Value-Added Tax Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods qualify for 0% VAT when the goods are physically exported from Korea and the export is supported by an approved customs export declaration. Services, including AI data labeling and BPO services, may qualify for 0% VAT when supplied to a non-resident recipient whose place of business is outside Korea and the service is not deemed supplied in Korea under the place-of-supply rules of the Value-Added Tax Act. The supplier must retain a written contract, evidence of the non-resident status of the recipient, and documentation showing that the consideration is received in foreign currency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (approved by Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS, including the Export Declaration Number)
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) proving physical export from Korea
Commercial Invoice and packing list matching the export declaration
Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation or Inward Remittance Certificate issued by an authorized foreign exchange bank, evidencing receipt of export proceeds in a convertible currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service electronically cross-match the approved customs export declaration, the zero-rated e-tax invoice, and bank foreign exchange receipts. If the physical export is found to be fictitious, the documentation is false, or the foreign exchange proceeds are not received within 180 calendar days from the export clearance date, the zero-rating is retrospectively revoked. The exporter will be assessed output VAT at 10% on the supply, plus statutory penalty surcharges and National Tax interest for underpayment based on the Framework Act on National Taxes. Deliberate documentation fraud triggers criminal penalties and the denial of input VAT refunds, and the responsible parties may be subject to criminal prosecution for tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), central bank and de jure monetary authority, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) jointly administering the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and prudential reporting framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a free-floating won with current-account convertibility broadly available to residents and non-residents; service export earnings from data-labeling and RLHF BPO can be received in KRW or foreign currency and converted at any licensed foreign exchange bank without prior licensing. The capital account remains subject to registration, reporting, or approval controls under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, especially for direct equity injections, external loans, and overseas payments exceeding the bank's presumed documentation threshold. There is no blanket surrender rule for service export proceeds, yet the bank must allocate every receipt to the correct transaction classification, apply the source-of-wealth probing rule, and retain underlying contracts and invoices for a minimum of seven years under AML obligations. Profit remittance is legally permitted, but requires audited or reviewed financial statements proving accumulated undistributed earnings, a corporate tax clearance certificate, the annual board resolution, and a foreign exchange bank's certificate showing the initial capital contribution was properly reported; until those documents are clean, remittances will be quarantined. The practical constraint is therefore documentary density and beneficiary KYC rather than administrative prohibition, and any failure to classify cross-border flows accurately can trigger FSS penalties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, export and service proceeds must be settled no later than one year from the date of export declaration or service completion; extensions are possible only with bank approval. For a Yuhan Hoesa engaging in cross-border AI data-labeling and RLHF BPO, 100% of invoice value must be repatriated to a licensed Korean bank's foreign-currency or KRW account; no mandatory sale-to-KRW ratio exists at present and the full amount can remain in a foreign-currency deposit, but any conversion is executed at the bank's prevailing rate and coded as service export settlement. The bank will treat a settlement exceeding one year as a compliance event and require a written explanation, supporting client correspondence, and a bank-approved trade-payment extension.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)
Capital Escrow Account for equity subscription and capital verification
Multi-Currency Operational and FX Settlement Account
Corporate Current Account with FX trade line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury rail and only conditional as an ancillary payout edge. Offshore digital EMIs such as Mass_PayPal_Payout, Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, or Revolut Business are not licensed as Korean foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and therefore cannot lawfully provide the primary KRW corporate account, perform Bank of Korea transaction reporting, or issue capital-verification certificates for a Yuhan Hoesa. They may be appended strictly as disbursement channels after funds are swept from a Shinhan or Hana operational account via a licensed cross-border transfer, with every batch carrying the appropriate foreign exchange purpose code and complete beneficiary KYC evidence. Using the EMI as the entity's main settlement rail would trigger a bank-account integrity alert and a likely rejection at the onboarding committee.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory director and all authorized signatories are required to appear physically at the flagship branch interview for the first corporate account opening because the Korean Real Name Financial Transactions Act prohibits anonymous account opening and most tier-1 banks mandate face-to-face verification for corporations with foreign shareholders. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for new accounts at Shinhan, Kookmin, Hana, or Woori. If a director cannot travel, the alternative is a notarial power of attorney to a Korean resident representative, who must appear in person with the original apostilled or consular-certified POA; the foreign director must still undergo live video verification in a bank-hosted virtual session during the same onboarding workflow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity caused by non-resident shareholders who route equity through one or more intermediary holding companies above the Yuhan Hoesa LLC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the ultimate parent company's certificate of incorporation, registry excerpt, or companies-formation file identifying the natural-person shareholder; apostilled or notarized statutory declaration of beneficial ownership and source of wealth for every natural person owning 25% or more; a diagram of all intermediate entities with certified copies of each entity's corporate registry; passport or national ID scans of all UBOs; and twelve months of bank reference letters from each intermediate entity's home bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bulk cross-border disbursements to a large distributed network of gig annotators through non-bank payout platforms are presumed to carry elevated money-laundering layering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A weekly payout ledger exported from Mass_PayPal_Payout and Wise with each beneficiary identified; the signed master services agreement with the end client; service invoices and proof-of-task metrics for a statistical sample of at least 10% of beneficiaries; individual worker KYC and contract packages for beneficiaries above the bank-set threshold; and a data protection impact assessment explaining the legal and operational rationale for using digital payout rails.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Triangular foreign-exchange flow between USD-denominated client invoices, KRW operating expenses, and multi-currency annotator payouts may replicate disguised round-tripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A treasury and trade reconciliation pack mapping every inbound USD settlement to corresponding outbound payroll and fixed-cost cash flows; signed service-level agreements listing per-unit pricing and billing milestones; a monthly FX exposure forecast; a twenty-four month trial balance with general ledger extracts; and bank-to-bank confirmation of the underlying trade function for both inflow and outflow counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A newly formed Yuhan Hoesa with no minimum paid-in capital presents thin-equity risk and a heightened shell-company formation concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A board-attested capital contribution statement supported by a Korean certified public accountant's capital verification report; the opening bank statement and SWIFT credit evidence for the shareholder remittance; the company tax registration certificate and corporate seal certificate; the first-year cash-flow budget and signed subscription agreement; and evidence of an operational office lease or registered business address in Korea.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inward equity injections must be executed as SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the UBO's home bank using the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act capital contribution classification. The remittance narrative must include the Yuhan Hoesa corporate registration number and the bank-assigned direct-investment-equity purpose code. After funds land in the Kookmin Bank Capital Escrow Account or Shinhan capital account, the bank will issue an internal capital verification certificate and file the transaction with the Bank of Korea external-transaction statistics system. The shareholder must deliver board minutes approving the funding, a capital subscription statement, and the certified corporate registration to satisfy the foreign exchange bank; any receivable exceeding approximately KRW 100 million requires the bank to retain the underlying subscription agreement and evidence of foreign-investment notification or registration with the relevant Korean authorities before the funds are available for current-account disbursement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For BPO trade settlements, use SWIFT MT103 direct transfers for corporate supplier payments, software procurement, and fees owed to overseas annotation intermediaries; each message must reference the commercial invoice and carry the service-export disbursement purpose code under ISIC 8220. For high-value hardware imports supporting AI processing, use an irrevocable Commercial LC with a sight draft and presentation of commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, and inspection certificate. Documentary Collections at sight are acceptable where the counterparty is well known and the bank has a prior credit relationship. For mass payouts to individual annotators, aggregate the KRW/USD operating balance into Mass_PayPal_Payout or Wise only after a licensed onshore bank has approved the disbursement batch, and reconcile every SWIFT MT103 or platform payout record back to the Korea-side bank statement reference number before month-end treasury settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore forward contracts in USD/KRW and EUR/KRW with tenors up to twelve months are permitted when supported by underlying service-export receivables or payroll liabilities, with no speculative gearing allowed.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only for residual offshore USD exposure that cannot be settled onshore; they must be executed through a licensed Korean bank treasury to remain enforceable and will be refused by the compliance committee if the underlying contract is absent.

Cross-currency swaps are allowed strictly as matched-cashflow treasury transactions for the exchange of USD/KRW amounts under confirmed AI BPO contract milestones; exotic options, barrier structures, and pure speculative overlays are excluded from the sanctioned hedging policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting of Members; approval of annual financial statements, profit appropriation, appointment of directors/auditor; minutes recorded in the Minute Book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No public registry filing is made; statutory corporate records are maintained at the company's registered office under the Korean Commercial Act (Yuhan Hoesa chapter)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year, by 31 March of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct filing penalty applies; non-convocation permits a member to request a court order, and directors may be subject to administrative fines under the Commercial Act; submitting the corporate income tax return without member-approved financial statements may trigger NTS non-filing surcharges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return with tax base, tax payable, local corporate income tax surtax, and controlling shareholder declaration annex
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of Korea; district tax office of jurisdiction and Hometax e-filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; by 31 March for a 31 December year-end; extended to 4 months by 30 April when a mandatory external audit applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing surtax of 20% of the unpaid tax; failure to file after a demand triggers an additional 10% surtax; fraudulent concealment or aggravated under-reporting triggers a 40% surtax; late-payment interest accrues at 0.022% per day; persistent non-filing and an inactive business presence may result in administrative cancellation of the business registration by the NTS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Mandatory external audit and certified auditor's report; filing of audited financial statements to DART when the statutory audit threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service via DART electronic disclosure; the external auditor is registered with the Financial Services Commission; private LLCs below the threshold retain the report at the registered office for member inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The external audit report must be completed before the Ordinary General Meeting; when electronic disclosure applies, audited financial statements must be filed within 4 months after fiscal year-end, or by 30 April for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Act on External Audit and Accounting, failure to appoint an external auditor when required may result in an administrative order and a fine of up to KRW 20 million; submission of false audited statements triggers auditor sanctions and criminal penalties; omission of a required audit also exposes the company to NTS reduced-penalty denial and unfaithful filing treatment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax returns for the first half-year, second half-year, and two preliminary VAT prepayment returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of Korea via local tax office or Hometax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half-year return due 25 July; second half-year return due 25 January; preliminary VAT prepayments due 25 April and 25 October
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a VAT return triggers a 20% additional tax on the unpaid amount; understated output VAT or excessive input VAT claims trigger a 10% surtax; failure to issue or submit tax invoices attracts a penalty of up to 2% of supply value, plus 0.022% daily arrears interest; repeated non-filing can lead to administrative closure of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer annual withholding summary and payment statements for wage and salary income, including year-end tax settlement data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of Korea; district tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual withholding schedule for wages paid in the prior calendar year is due by 10 February of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit, or false submission of, wage payment statements carries a penalty of KRW 20,000 per employee statement plus 10% of the withheld amount if not remitted; wilful non-remittance may subject the responsible director to criminal prosecution and NTS business registration cancellation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Yuhan Hoesa is subject to mandatory independent certified audit under the Act on External Audit and Accounting and its Presidential Decree if: (1) total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12 billion, approximately USD 8.9 million at KRW 1,350 per USD, regardless of revenue and headcount; or (2) total assets are between KRW 5 billion and KRW 12 billion and the company meets at least two of the following three quantitative tests: annual revenue of at least KRW 10 billion, total assets at fiscal year-end of at least KRW 8 billion, or average monthly employees of at least 100; or (3) the company is a listed corporation or designated by the Financial Services Commission. Even below these statutory triggers, a Korean bank or AML-regulated counterparty may contractually require an independent audit for financing or ongoing KYC confidence.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korea International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) applies to listed companies and specified public entities; private non-listed companies apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP / Korean Accounting Standards for Non-Public Entities); financial statements must be prepared in Korean won and in the Korean language, with English working papers acceptable for parent reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Yuhan Hoesa is a private LLC and has no separate public UBO annual return to the Korean corporate registry. Beneficial ownership is disclosed annually inside the corporate income tax return through the controlling shareholder and special-relationship annex filed with the NTS. Any transfer of membership quotas must be entered in the register of members to be effective against the company; if the transfer changes the controlling shareholder, the register must be updated promptly and the tax annex must be updated at the next filing. There is no general statutory 30-day government filing window for private LLC quota transfers, but if the company maintains a Korean business bank account, the bank's AML and customer due diligence framework will require the company to notify the bank within 30 days of a 20% or more change in beneficial ownership, and the bank will require an annual KYC refresh.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Mortgages and Charges over membership interests and company assets
Minute Book containing members' general meetings and director or manager meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - 1,500 per annum for a standard Korean corporate secretarial agent and registered office address, including handling NTS notices and statutory register maintenance; higher with full outsourcing
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 - 18,000 per annum for a certified Korean statutory audit for an AI data-labeling BPO, depending on ERP complexity, intercompany transactions, staffing volume, and audit-deadline urgency; if the statutory threshold is not met, external audit cost would be USD 0 unless a counterparty contractually requires it.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% national corporate income tax on the first KRW 200 million of taxable income, 19% on the next KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion tranche, 21% on the KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion tranche, and 24% above KRW 300 billion; a 10% local income tax surcharge is added, producing an effective first-tier headline rate of 9.9% plus an aggregate effective top rate of 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible technology and foreign-invested projects may access Tax Incentive Limitation Law credits, including up to 25% R&D tax credits on qualifying artificial-intelligence data-curation research expenditure, SME employment and facility investment credits, and Free Economic Zone tax holidays for qualifying high-tech foreign direct investment (100% corporate income tax exemption for five years and a 50% reduction for two further years); no patent box regime applies to AI data-labeling output, but employment-linked credits can reduce effective rates below the headline tier for qualifying SMEs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return and Tax Base Statement (Form No. 1) together with the Foreign Corporation Income Tax Return Annex where the company is foreign-owned; filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal, with the Balance Sheet, Income Statement, comprehensive related-party transaction schedules, and withholding reconciliation annexed.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; corporations with prior-year tax liability must also pay semi-annual interim corporate income tax within two months of the end of the first six-month period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within three months after the close of the fiscal year; a calendar-year AI/BPO entity must file by March 31 of the following year; interim tax is payable by August 31 for a calendar-year entity; no blanket extension is available and late filings accrue penalties from the statutory due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification block: corporate registration number, legal name, representative director, registered head office address, business place, fiscal year-end, and business activity code (ISIC 8220/NAICS 518210).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Exact Korean registration number for the Yuhan Hoesa LLC and the ultimate foreign parent's name, country, and tax identification; failure to disclose the offshore parent triggers economic-substance review; a foreign parent's Tax Residency Certificate should be attached only if treaty-reduced withholding is claimed on later boxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from AI training-data services: bounding-box annotation, computer-vision labeling, RLHF data curation, quality assurance, and BPO service fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report accrual-basis revenue for all work performed by Korean staff for foreign clients; PayPal and Wise settlement inflows are not a legal basis for deferring revenue; the NTS compares bank data with invoices, and any instruction to split revenue to foreign accounts is a criminal-evasion red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales: direct wages of annotators and data taggers, outsourced labeling subcontract costs, cloud AI infrastructure hosting, hardware depreciation, and direct data-processing consumables.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border subcontractor costs must be supported by valid contracts, invoices, and proof of actual service performance; intercompany subcontract fees must be priced at arm's length; if services are merely shifted to a zero-tax related entity, the NTS will disallow the deduction and recharacterize the payment as a constructive dividend or royalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit: gross revenue less cost of sales; the gross margin is the starting point for transfer-pricing screening.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compare the gross margin to the Korean entity's economic functions and risks; if the entity lacks staff, premises, or decision-making substance, the NTS may apply Transaction Net Margin Method or Profit Split to impute more Korean-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general, and administrative expenses: local payroll, rent, utilities, marketing, legal and accounting fees, software subscriptions, and head-office management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees, branding fees, and shared-service charges from the foreign parent require benefit-test documentation and Core Income-Generating Activity substance; payments for services not actually rendered or duplicating local functions are non-deductible and may be reclassified as dividends subject to withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income: interest on deposits, foreign exchange gains, dividends received, rental income, insurance proceeds, and other incidental income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all passive Korean-source income; outbound interest and royalties paid to the foreign parent must be separately disclosed on the withholding schedule; treaty-reduced rates must be substantiated, otherwise the statutory 22% withholding is due.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating expenses: intercompany loan interest, foreign exchange losses, donations, penalties, and other non-operating deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest on loans from a foreign related-party is tested against Korea's thin-capitalization rules; excessive interest may be denied and recharacterized as a dividend; fines, criminal penalties, and taxes are not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before loss carryforward: gross income less deductible expenses and adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recompute with all transfer-pricing adjustments, add back non-deductible expenses, and verify whether the Korean entity is a resident domestic corporation or a non-resident with a permanent establishment; a stripped-margin Korean entity faces audit adjustments and penalty surcharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward deduction: net operating losses from prior fiscal years, with ownership continuity schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach NOL computation schedules and confirm shareholding continuity; the NTS scrutinizes loss utilization after cross-border reorganizations and may deny deductions if the business was not substantially continued.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base: taxable income after loss carryforward, subject to progressive rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the tiered rates and calculate the local income tax surcharge at 10% of national tax; the foreign parent cannot consolidate Korean profits overseas and cannot use the local loss unless filed and accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory corporate income tax calculation: national tax computed on the tax base plus the 10% local income tax surcharge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean entity has been a permanent establishment of a foreign enterprise, tax is computed on its domestic-business attributable income; the annual return must present an arm's-length profit allocation for the AI/BPO functions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits and prepayments: R&D credits, employment credits, foreign tax credits, interim tax prepayments, and withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean LLC is the taxpayer claiming credits; the foreign parent's tax attributes cannot be transferred into the Korean return; any foreign tax credit claimed must be supported by foreign tax payment receipts and treaty articles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund: total corporate income tax less credits and prepayments, plus additional taxes and overdue surcharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the net liability electronically to the National Tax Service before filing; an outstanding balance above the enforcement threshold leads to asset seizure, travel ban, and blacklisting of the representative director.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 20% no-return penalty on the unpaid corporate tax, a 10% understatement penalty for negligent misreporting, and a 40% additional penalty for fraudulent underreporting; late payment accrues approximately 0.03% per day as late-payment surcharge; willful tax evasion is criminally prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment up to five years and fines up to three times the evaded tax, while persistent non-compliance leads to collection enforcement, business premises seizure, and director blacklisting.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% on outbound cash or constructive dividends: 20% national withholding tax under the Corporate Tax Act plus the 10% local income tax surcharge (i.e., 20% + 2% local withholding), absent treaty reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim bilateral Double Tax Treaty relief, the Korean payer must, prior to making the remittance, obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign treaty jurisdiction, a beneficial ownership declaration, evidence that the recipient is not a conduit or agent, and any Limitation-on-Benefits certificate required by the treaty; the withholding agent must submit the Non-Resident Tax Treaty Exemption/Reduction application through HomeTax and retain the original documentation for at least five years, and if treaty relief is denied the statutory 22% withholding must be remitted or the shareholder may pursue a refund claim after proving entitlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on outbound royalties and interest is 22% (20% national plus 2% local surcharge); treaty rates generally reduce royalties and interest to 10% to 15%, with many Korean DTAs providing a 10% rate for beneficial owners in treaty jurisdictions (e.g., Korea-US royalty and interest at 10%); the reduced rate is unavailable unless the beneficial ownership and residency proofs are filed before or with the payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File and Local File are statutorily required when annual consolidated revenue reaches KRW 100 billion and foreign related-party transactions exceed KRW 50 billion; all corporations with cross-border related-party transactions above de minimis levels must file the disclosure form, and the NTS can request contemporaneous local documentation within 45 to 60 days for taxpayers carrying lower transaction volumes if audit risk is identified.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the International Tax Adjustment Act and National Tax Basic Act Article 14 impose a substance-over-form rule: a foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa must have real Korean offices, local payroll, operational management, and Core Income-Generating Activities for annotation, labeling, RLHF curation, and client contracting; if decision-making and personnel reside abroad and the Korean entity merely passes income and expenses, the NTS will recharacterize the entity as a shell, disregard its separate personality, attribute income to the foreign parent, and apply Controlled Foreign Company rules to offshore retained earnings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion / false corporate income tax filing and offshore revenue concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directing non-Korean AI clients to remit PayPal/Wise payments to offshore accounts, omitting Korean-source revenue from the Corporate Income Tax Return, issuing forged invoices or no invoices, and filing a nil return while the Korean entity's bank accounts receive funds for annotation and RLHF services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3(1) imposes imprisonment up to five years or a fine up to three times the evaded tax; the Corporate Tax Act imposes a 20% no-return penalty, 10% negligent understatement penalty, and 40% fraudulent understatement penalty; the National Tax Collection Act adds late-payment surcharge of about 0.03% per day until full settlement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts may pierce the corporate veil when the Yuhan Hoesa is used as a mere instrumentality: the representative director is jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax, local tax, penalties, and accrued interest; personal bank accounts and overseas assets can be attached; the NTS may blacklist the director, impose a travel ban, block exit at the airport, and revoke passports; criminal conviction carries imprisonment and disqualification from future corporate directorships.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial profit shifting / shell company lacking economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing the Korean LLC only to sign AI data-labeling contracts while outsourced related entities in zero-tax jurisdictions perform or falsely claim to perform the actual annotation work, paying inflated intercompany fees for nonexistent algorithm development or management services, and booking continuous Korean tax losses without any local employees, premises, client contracting, or operational substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: International Tax Adjustment Act Article 5 authorizes the National Tax Service to adjust the transaction to an arm's-length price and impute profits to the Korean entity; CFC and GAAR rules reattribute passive offshore retained earnings; transfer-pricing penalty surcharges of up to 20% of adjusted taxaable income and daily late-payment penalties apply, together with refusal to grant deductions for bogus service fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under National Tax Basic Act Article 39, directors who actually exercise control over funds and assets may be secondarily liable for the corporate tax when the company's assets are insufficient; Commercial Act Article 399 exposes directors to civil damages; aggravating conduct is punished as aiding tax evasion and loots the corporate veil protection, resulting in personal asset restitution, travel bans, and criminal imprisonment for direct participants.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-withholding / abusive tax treaty relief on profit repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, technology royalties, or intercompany interest to the foreign parent without withholding the statutory 22%, submitting a forged or stale Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial-ownership declaration to use a treaty rate, or recharacterizing royalties as cost reimbursements or data-service fees solely to avoid Korean withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Tax Act Articles 98 and 98-5 require withholding on outbound dividends, interest, and royalties; failure to withhold triggers a demand against the withholding agent for the full amount plus negligence surcharges of 10% to 40% and late-payment interest; willful non-collection is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with fines up to three times the evaded tax and imprisonment up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director and finance director who knowingly fail to withhold are personally liable for the unremitted withholding tax if the company cannot pay; Korean tax courts and civil courts allow veil-piercing where the directors diverted funds to themselves or the foreign parent; they face personal asset seizure, blacklisting, exit bans, and criminal conviction, while the foreign parent may lose treaty benefits and be exposed to a permanent Korean withholding obligation on future distributions.
